settings.content:
Where the wisdom of Scripture meets careful craft.

Anointing with oil runs through the whole of Scripture: the horn of oil that anointed David, the oil of gladness of the Psalms, the alabaster jar broken at Bethany. Many of our oils are made with the plants, resins, and extracts those pages name, revered for millennia: frankincense, myrrh, spikenard, hyssop, pomegranate, and rose of Sharon.

We prepare them with care in a base of olive squalane and olive oil, so that an oil made for prayer, worship, and blessing also nourishes the skin. This page explains what is in every bottle.

settings.title: Naturally derived actives
settings.content: Every active compound comes from a plant, resin, fruit, or seed. We do not synthesize our actives in a lab.

settings.title: No parabens, no sulfates
settings.content: Free from parabens, phthalates, sulfates, and synthetic fragrances. We exclude ingredients that do not align with our values.

settings.title: Non-comedogenic
settings.content: Formulated to nourish the skin without clogging pores.

settings.title: Cruelty-free
settings.content: We honor all of God’s creation and never test on animals.

settings.title: Transparent and thoughtful
settings.content: Packaging chosen with care for God’s creation. Every compound published with its botanical origin.

settings.title: The plants come first
settings.content: The plants, resins, and extracts that Scripture names, revered for millennia, are where every product begins.

settings.title: The plant’s own compounds
settings.content: The actives are extracted, purified, and concentrated from the plants themselves, the same botanical sources God placed in creation, not made in a laboratory.

settings.title: The oil of Scripture
settings.content: Each extract is carried in 100% olive-derived squalane, from the tree that lit the tabernacle and anointed kings. A light, stable oil, with no chemical solvents or artificial emulsifiers.

settings.title: For prayer, worship, and blessing
settings.content: An oil for the moments Scripture describes: consecration, intercession, worship, and prayer for healing. It honors that tradition and nourishes the skin.

settings.title: Olive squalane base
settings.content:
We formulate our anointing oils in a base of 100% olive-derived squalane and olive oil. Squalane is a naturally occurring lipid closely related to the squalene found in human skin.

Squalane is a light, stable oil. It spreads easily, carries the botanical extracts with it, and leaves the skin feeling hydrated rather than greasy. We use no chemical solvents or artificial emulsifiers.

Squalane comes from the fruit of the olive tree: the oil that lit the lamps of the tabernacle (Exodus 27:20) and the oil with which Samuel anointed David (1 Samuel 16:13). Our name comes from the same tree: the Mount of Olives, where Jesus prayed in the garden of Gethsemane.

Shop 100% Squalane

settings.title: The polyphenol complex
settings.content:
Central to every Mount of Olives anointing oil is Polyphenol Alpha (α)™, our proprietary antioxidant-rich polyphenol complex, derived entirely from natural botanical sources. It brings together several families of plant polyphenols: flavonoids, phenolic acids, stilbenes, and lignans.

Polyphenol Alpha (α)™ is not a single ingredient. It is a blend of many compounds working together, much the way Scripture describes the body: “many members, yet but one body” (1 Corinthians 12:20).

Read the full ingredient glossary

settings.title: The botanicals
settings.content:
Every active compound in our formulations is a natural derivative of a plant, resin, fruit, or seed with deep biblical significance. We do not synthesize our actives in a laboratory. We extract, purify, and concentrate them from the same botanical sources that God placed in creation.

  • Boswellic acids from Boswellia serrata (frankincense), the resin of the Magi
  • Terpenoids and sesquiterpenes from Commiphora myrrha (myrrh), the resin of purification
  • Ellagitannins and punicalagins from Punica granatum (pomegranate), one of the seven blessed fruits of the Promised Land
  • Hydroxytyrosol and oleuropein from Olea europaea (olive), the tree of peace
  • Apigenin and flavonoids from Hyssopus officinalis (hyssop), the herb of purification (Psalm 51:7)
  • Jatamansone and sesquiterpenes from Nardostachys jatamansi (spikenard), the precious oil of Mary of Bethany
  • Labdanum and polyphenols from Cistus ladaniferus (rose of Sharon), the flower of Song of Solomon

These are not synthetic analogs or lab-created substitutes. They are the natural constituents of the very plants Scripture names: extracted, concentrated, and blended into our oils.

settings.title: Our standards
settings.content:
We believe that what we place on our bodies, temples of the Holy Spirit, deserves the highest standards of purity and care. Our commitment:

  • 100% naturally derived active ingredients. Every active compound originates from a botanical source.
  • Free from parabens, phthalates, sulfates, and synthetic fragrances. We exclude ingredients that do not align with our values.
  • Non-comedogenic formulation. Made to nourish the skin without clogging pores.
  • Cruelty-free. We honor all of God’s creation and never test on animals.
  • Thoughtful packaging. Chosen with care, as part of our stewardship of the earth.
  • Full ingredient transparency. We publish every compound and its botanical origin, because we believe informed customers are empowered customers.

settings.title: Olive
settings.content:
Olea europaea

The tree of peace, and the tree of Gethsemane. Its oil anointed kings and priests. Our squalane base and its polyphenols, hydroxytyrosol and oleuropein, come from its fruit.

settings.title: Frankincense
settings.content:
Boswellia serrata

A symbol of prayer rising before God like incense, and a gift of the Magi (Matthew 2:11). Its resin gives us boswellic acids.

settings.title: Myrrh
settings.content:
Commiphora myrrha

A symbol of purification and of Christ’s sacrifice, and a gift of the Magi. Its resin gives us terpenoids and sesquiterpenes.

settings.title: Pomegranate
settings.content:
Punica granatum

A symbol of fruitfulness and abundance, one of the seven blessed fruits of the Promised Land (Deuteronomy 8:8). Its fruit and seed give us ellagitannins and punicalagins.

settings.title: Hyssop
settings.content:
Hyssopus officinalis

The herb of purification: “Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean” (Psalm 51:7). It gives us apigenin and other flavonoids.

settings.title: Spikenard
settings.content:
Nardostachys jatamansi

The precious oil Mary of Bethany poured out in extravagant worship (John 12:3). Its root gives us jatamansone and sesquiterpenes.

settings.title: Rose of Sharon
settings.content:
Cistus ladaniferus

“I am the rose of Sharon” (Song of Solomon 2:1). The labdanum shrub of the Mediterranean, rich in polyphenols.

settings.title: Lily of the Valley
settings.content:
Symbol of purity and peace

“I am the rose of Sharon, and the lily of the valleys” (Song of Solomon 2:1). Our Lily of the Valley oil is made for devotion and prayer.

settings.title: The plants Scripture names
settings.content: Every product in our collection begins with these plants, each with its own place in Scripture. Tap a botanical to shop its oil.

settings.content: Every oil is built on the same olive squalane base. Tap a bottle to see the oil and add it to your cart.

settings.question: Hydroxytyrosol
settings.answer: A polyphenol found mainly in olives and olive oil. An antioxidant.

settings.question: Tyrosol
settings.answer: A phenolic antioxidant found in olives, olive oil, and wine.

settings.question: Oleuropein-aglycone dialdehyde
settings.answer: A secoiridoid polyphenol from olives. An antioxidant.

settings.question: Oleuropein-aglycone mono-aldehyde
settings.answer: A closely related olive secoiridoid, also an antioxidant, that rounds out the olive polyphenols in our formulations.

settings.question: Ligstroside-aglycone di-aldehyde
settings.answer: A secoiridoid compound found in olives and extra virgin olive oil. An antioxidant.

settings.question: Pinoresinol
settings.answer: A lignan found in olives, olive oil, and sesame seeds. An antioxidant.

settings.question: Olive oil (Olea europaea)
settings.answer: Cold-pressed from the fruit of the olive tree. Rich in oleic acid, squalene, hydroxytyrosol, and tocopherols. A nourishing emollient and the natural source of the compounds at the heart of our Polyphenol Alpha (α)™ complex.

settings.question: Squalane (olive-derived)
settings.answer: A fully saturated, stable hydrocarbon made by hydrogenating squalene from Olea europaea (olive). Closely related to the squalene naturally present in human skin, it is a light emollient that leaves the skin feeling hydrated, not greasy. Non-comedogenic, odorless, and oxidatively stable: the carrier for our Polyphenol Alpha (α)™ complex.

settings.question: Boswellia serrata (frankincense)
settings.answer: A resin from the bark of the Boswellia serrata tree, native to India and the Middle East. It contains boswellic acids (AKBA and KBA). One of the three gifts the Magi presented to the Christ child (Matthew 2:11), and a cornerstone ingredient in ancient anointing formulations.

settings.question: Commiphora myrrha (myrrh)
settings.answer: An oleoresin harvested from the Commiphora myrrha tree of the Arabian Peninsula and northeastern Africa. It contains terpenoids (curzerene, furanoeudesma-1,3-diene), sesquiterpenes, and flavonoids. A gift of the Magi and a biblical symbol of purification, consecration, and healing.

settings.question: Botanical resins
settings.answer: Natural oleoresins from frankincense, myrrh, and labdanum: complex mixtures of terpenes, sesquiterpenes, and phenolic acids, used in traditional formulations for millennia.

settings.question: Hyssopus officinalis (hyssop)
settings.answer: The biblical herb of purification named in Psalm 51:7: “Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean.” It contains apigenin, rosmarinic acid, and essential oil terpenes.

settings.question: Nardostachys jatamansi (spikenard)
settings.answer: The precious aromatic rhizome Mary of Bethany used to anoint Jesus before his burial (John 12:3). It contains jatamansone, nardosinone, and sesquiterpenes. One of the rarest and most valued botanicals in our collection.

settings.question: Cistus ladaniferus (rose of Sharon)
settings.answer: The labdanum-producing Mediterranean shrub referenced as the rose of Sharon in Song of Solomon 2:1. Rich in polyphenols.

settings.question: Punica granatum (pomegranate)
settings.answer: One of the seven species blessed in the Torah (Deuteronomy 8:8). The fruit and seed contain ellagitannins, punicalagins A and B, punicalin, gallic acid, and ellagic acid, all polyphenols.

settings.question: Ellagitannins
settings.answer: Tannins found in pomegranates, raspberries, and walnuts. Antioxidant polyphenols.

settings.question: Apigenin
settings.answer: A flavonoid naturally present in parsley (Petroselinum crispum), chamomile (Matricaria chamomilla), celery (Apium graveolens), and hyssop (Hyssopus officinalis). An antioxidant.

settings.question: Caffeic acid
settings.answer: A hydroxycinnamic acid found in coffee, wine, and many plants. An antioxidant.

settings.question: Catechin
settings.answer: A flavan-3-ol polyphenol abundant in tea (Camellia sinensis) and many fruits. An antioxidant.

settings.question: Chlorogenic acid
settings.answer: A phenolic compound found in coffee and stone fruits. An antioxidant.

settings.question: Epicatechin
settings.answer: A flavanol found in tea and cocoa. An antioxidant.

settings.question: Ferulic acid
settings.answer: A phenolic compound from rice bran, wheat, and oats. An antioxidant. A key component of our Polyphenol Alpha (α)™ complex.

settings.question: Gallic acid
settings.answer: A trihydroxybenzoic acid found in grapes, tea leaves, and oak bark. An antioxidant.

settings.question: Homovanillic acid
settings.answer: A phenolic compound found in vanilla beans and select botanical sources. An antioxidant.

settings.question: Isoquercitrin
settings.answer: A quercetin glycoside found in apples, onions, and various plants. An antioxidant.

settings.question: Luteolin
settings.answer: A flavone found in celery, parsley, and thyme. An antioxidant.

settings.question: Quercetin
settings.answer: One of the most abundant dietary flavonoids, found in apples, onions, berries, and tea. An antioxidant.

settings.question: Quercitrin (quercetin-3-rhamnoside)
settings.answer: A quercetin glycoside found in citrus fruits and berries. An antioxidant.

settings.question: Rutin
settings.answer: A flavonoid glycoside found in buckwheat, apples, and citrus. An antioxidant.
